summary: Single-sourced the site canonical origin: tools/site/templates.mjs now derives BASE_URL from REA_SITE_URL with the GitHub Pages origin that package.json homepage and .github/workflows/pages.yml actually deploy, tests assert against that one source plus the package homepage instead of a duplicated Vercel literal, and the regenerated site fixed canonical/OG/sitemap/robots. Verified the npm package surface (369 files) and CLI version (0.3.2) match the same sources.
checksNotRun: No live deploy was performed (GitHub Pages and Vercel both require maintainer approval).
Vercel is still documented as an optional second host; the site was not rebuilt or verified against that deployment.
No browser rendering check of the rebuilt pages.
decisions: The canonical origin is GitHub Pages because that is what the deploy workflow and package.json homepage already publish; Vercel stays available only through REA_SITE_URL at build time.
Tests import BASE_URL instead of restating a domain, so changing the host is one edit and cannot silently desync canonical/OG/sitemap/robots.
risks: Google Search Console and any inbound links may still index the Vercel host; switching canonical affects SEO and needs maintainer awareness.
All generated pages under site/ were rebuilt, so the diff is large even though the substantive change is the origin plus test wiring.
Changes are worktree-only until committed; npm publish and Pages deploy are not part of this task.
recommendedNextAction: Commit the canonical-origin change and, after the next Pages deploy, confirm the served /sitemap.xml and canonical tags resolve on enzovezzaro.github.io/rea-faang.
